provenance.notes: Mid-size edu batch. Written for an institute director or marketing and admissions lead; leaned on the course catalogue with intake dates, enrolment with payment and the corporate training funnel. Corporate client portal and student portal ranges are the least certain.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Every course searchable by field, level, mode (classroom, online, blended), duration, campus and next intake, each with fees, seats left, entry requirements and an enrol button
pageStructurePlus.why: Learners compare institutes course by course, not by homepage. The one that shows the next intake date and price for the exact course gets the enquiry.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Courses delivered at the client's site or online, custom programmes, group rates, trainer profiles, how attendance and completion are reported, and a training request form
pageStructurePlus.why: One company booking can fill a whole cohort. Learning and development managers need a page to forward internally and a way to request a proposal.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Prerequisites per course, an online placement or language level test, recognition of prior learning, and what happens if a learner doesn't meet the bar yet
pageStructurePlus.why: Adult learners fear signing up for the wrong level. A placement test online turns that doubt into an enrolment on the right course.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Instalment options per course, employer-paid invoicing, a sponsorship letter template, refund and deferral terms, and funding schemes where the institute is eligible
pageStructurePlus.why: Many vocational learners can't pay a course fee in one go, and many have employers willing to pay. Both need the terms in writing before they enrol.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Exam dates and booking, what the certificate is and who issues it, accreditation details as placeholders until confirmed, and a certificate verification page for employers
pageStructurePlus.why: Learners enrol for the certificate, and employers check it. Showing how certification works, and letting employers verify it, is the institute's credibility.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Placement and careers support, employers who hire the institute's graduates where they agree to be named, and graduate stories shared with written consent
pageStructurePlus.why: Vocational learners are buying a job, not a course. They want to see the route into work without promises the institute can't keep.

designDirections.name: Next Intake
designDirections.bestFor: Institutes with a few flagship courses where the job is the next intake date and an enquiry or enrol button
designDirections.headlineSample: Career courses in {City}. Next intake starts soon.
designDirections.whyItFits: Citrus Morning feels energetic and practical, and the type-led hero puts the next intake date and the enrol button where a learner looks first.

designDirections.name: Course Catalogue
designDirections.bestFor: Institutes with many courses across fields and campuses that need a searchable catalogue with intakes and online enrolment
designDirections.headlineSample: Find your course and next intake in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family combo: Sky Kite reads as a children's school, and these learners are adults. Cobalt Wire is crisp and businesslike, and cards carry each course.

designDirections.name: Corporate Academy
designDirections.bestFor: Institutes where corporate training and in-house programmes bring in most of the revenue
designDirections.headlineSample: Training programmes for {City} teams and organisations
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy and brass read like a board report, which is who signs corporate training budgets, and the editorial serif gives proposals weight.

openers.line: Your course list is a PDF brochure, so someone searching a specific certification course in {City} can't land on a page for it with the fee and next intake.
openers.hook: Find the courses link. If it opens a PDF, or one page lists everything, the angle holds. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A course catalogue with a page per course and intake: {demo-link}

openers.line: The intake dates on your institute's course pages are from an earlier term. A learner ready to enrol now assumes the course isn't running.
openers.hook: Compare intake dates on the site with their latest posts. Note one course where they disagree.
openers.linkLine: Course pages with intake dates that update themselves: {demo-link}

openers.line: Enrolling on one of your courses means filling an enquiry form and waiting for an advisor to call. Working adults decide on a training course at night and want to secure the seat then.
openers.hook: Try to enrol on a course. Note where it stops: an enquiry form, a phone number, a visit-us line.
openers.linkLine: Online course enrolment with a seat held on payment: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your institute site was slow to open on my phone and the course search didn't fit the screen. Most learners browse courses on a phone during a commute or a break.
openers.hook: Load the homepage and a course page on mobile data. Note the seconds and what broke.
openers.linkLine: The same courses, quick and searchable on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts mention training teams for local companies, but the site has no corporate training page. A learning and development manager needs something to forward internally.
openers.hook: Look for 'corporate', 'in-house' or 'for business' on the site. Note whether there's a page or just a line.
openers.linkLine: A corporate training page with a proposal request: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find fees for any of your courses, only 'contact us for pricing'. Learners comparing two institutes for the same certification shortlist the one that shows a price.
openers.hook: Check three course pages for a fee or 'from' price. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Course pages with fees and payment plans: {demo-link}

openers.line: To find the right language or skill level at your institute I'd have to come in for a placement test. Adults choosing a course at night want to know their level before they visit.
openers.hook: Strongest for language institutes. Look for an online level test. If it's in-person only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: An online placement test that suggests the right course: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your graduates' reviews mention trainers by name and how the course helped them at work, but none of it appears on the course pages new learners read.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about a trainer or a course. Quote it if they reply.

openers.line: Your institute has more than one campus, but courses don't say where they run. A learner across town needs to know which campus and which evenings.
openers.hook: Count their campuses from map listings, in words. Check whether course pages show the campus.
openers.linkLine: Courses filterable by campus and timetable: {demo-link}

openers.line: I saw you're looking for trainers for the institute, but the site has no page for them. Industry practitioners decide whether to teach with you from how you present the role.
openers.hook: Find their trainer or assessor job posts. Check the site for a teach-with-us page. Note the field.
openers.linkLine: A teach-with-us page for trainers and assessors: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your graduates list your certificate on their CVs, but employers have no way to check it on your site. A verification page makes every certificate you issue more credible.
openers.hook: Search the site for verification or certificate check. Note whether one exists.
openers.linkLine: A certificate verification page for employers: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your classrooms and workshops look current in every post, but the institute's site looks older than the skills it teaches.
openers.hook: Compare a recent classroom or workshop post to the homepage. Note one dated thing.
openers.linkLine: A site that looks like the institute does now: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your next intake is a few weeks away, and the course pages still say 'enquire'. Learners deciding this month need to see seats left and how to secure one.
openers.hook: Find the next intake in their posts. Use in the weeks before it starts. Name the course.
openers.linkLine: An intake page with seats left and online enrolment: {demo-link}

openers.line: Many of your learners could get their employer to pay for the course, but nothing on the site explains invoicing or gives them a letter to take to their manager.
openers.hook: Look for 'employer-sponsored', 'company pays' or invoicing details. Note whether any exist.
openers.linkLine: An employer sponsorship page with a ready letter: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} at the institute looked like a proud day for the graduates. A cohort moment like that should live on the course pages, not only in a feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest event: a graduation, a cohort completing, a new workshop opening. Name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That institute moment, kept on the site: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} at the institute looked like a proud day for the graduates.

I looked at the {Business Name} site and noticed the courses sit in a PDF and enrolling stops at an enquiry form. I put together a sample with a searchable course catalogue, intake dates, online enrolment and a corporate training page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a course catalogue with fees and next intakes, an online placement test, enrolment with payment plans, a corporate training page and a certificate verification page. It feeds the student system you already use. If it's not the right time, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites and software for training institutes in {City}. I sent a sample for {Business Name} a few days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: a page per course with intake dates and fees, online enrolment and a corporate training page. Who else should see it, admissions or the corporate sales lead?"

IF YES:
"What did you and the team make of it?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"It works alongside your student and learning systems, it doesn't replace them. The build runs {Build Range} depending on the number of courses, campuses and integrations, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, intake updates and changes. For your institute I'd expect about {Build Price}."
"Could we do thirty minutes with you and whoever runs enrolments next week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a scope and a deposit invoice, timed so the catalogue is live before your next intake."

objections.objection: Our advisors close enrolments on the phone.
objections.handler: "Keep them. The site books the advisor call with the learner's course, level and budget already filled in, and lets the ready ones enrol and pay straight away."

objections.objection: We get most learners from education fairs and agents.
objections.handler: "Those learners still check the course page before they pay. The catalogue is what confirms the fair conversation, and the corporate page opens a funnel agents don't reach."

objections.objection: Our learning platform already has a course list.
objections.handler: "It runs the teaching well. It doesn't rank a course page for someone searching that certification in {City}. The site sends enrolled learners straight into it."

objections.objection: Fees change by intake, so we can't publish them.
objections.handler: "Fees can update per intake from one place. Show the current one with a 'from' price for the next, and learners stop ruling you out for not knowing."
"You do, and it describes the institute. The gap is the course: its own page, its fee, its next intake and a way to enrol. That's what people search for."

objections.objection: Accreditation rules limit what we can say.
objections.handler: "Good, that keeps it honest. Accreditation details go in exactly as issued, there are no job or pass promises, and nothing goes live without your sign-off."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's the course catalogue, enrolment and the corporate funnel. One company booking a cohort covers most of it."

email.subject: Course catalogue and enrolment for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for training institutes in {City}, and I made a sample for {Business Name} with a course catalogue, intake dates and online enrolment. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} course catalogue sample down on Friday to free up the space.

Should I keep it up for the team? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, learners start comparing courses a month or two before each intake, and companies plan training budgets for the year ahead. Thought of you.

The course catalogue sample is still here if you want another look: {demo-link}

bullets: Price by the number of courses, campuses and integrations, not pages. Course pages are templated; enrolment with payment is the work.
Peg the build to a few course fees or one corporate cohort. That's how the director already measures a good month.
Quote the site as the front door to their student and learning systems, never as a replacement for either.
Price the corporate funnel separately. It's a different buyer, and it often justifies the whole build on its own.
Time launches to the intake calendar, live several weeks before the next intake, never in its final week.
Never write pass rates, job placement promises or accreditation claims. Use what the institute provides, in placeholders until confirmed.

lineItems.item: Online enrolment with payment and instalments
lineItems.description: Max with instalment plans, employer invoicing, document upload and handoff to the student system.
Max when results suggest a course and intake, and an advisor gets the score with the learner's goals.

Max when employers check a certificate by code against the institute's records, with an audit log.

lineItems.item: Accessibility review of catalogue and enrolment

whatElseYouSell.name: Intake campaigns by course
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Search and social ads for the courses with seats left, pointing at each course page, timed to each intake and paused when the cohort fills."
whatElseYouSell.when: Six to eight weeks before each intake. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for each campus
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each campus profile kept current with next intakes, open evenings and course news, so people searching for training nearby see an active institute."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30. Priced by the number of campuses.

whatElseYouSell.name: Classroom and workshop photo and video day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A day filming practical training in the workshops and classrooms, only learners who sign a release, so each course page shows the real equipment."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a practical training day, with releases collected first.

whatElseYouSell.name: Graduate review and story programme
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Graduates are asked for a review when they receive their certificate, and longer stories go on the course pages only with written consent."
whatElseYouSell.when: After the first cohort enrolled through the site completes.

whatElseYouSell.name: Corporate training sales deck and case pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A deck and short case pages for the institute's corporate sales lead, written from client programmes with each client's permission."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the corporate section is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Open evening and info session campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An info session page, booking, reminders and a follow-up with the enrol link, for each training course's next open evening."
whatElseYouSell.when: Three to four weeks before each intake.

whatElseYouSell.name: Course brochure redesign for web and print
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Course content written once and published as catalogue pages and a printed brochure for education fairs, so the two never disagree."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, before the next fair season.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly learner newsletter
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A monthly email to past enquirers and graduates with upcoming intakes, next-level courses and short skill tips from the institute's trainers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the enquiry list is collected through the site.

withoutAI.route: Recruitment agencies placing the institute's graduates
withoutAI.whoPays: The recruitment agency, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agency that places your graduates in jobs takes CVs by email. A jobs board and candidate registration site would help them and your learners."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agencies value the institute as a candidate source, and the institute's introduction is a warm one.

withoutAI.route: Student accommodation providers near the campus
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The residence your out-of-town learners stay in takes bookings by phone. Room booking by intake dates would fill it every course cycle."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Housing providers depend on the institute's intakes and would welcome its recommendation.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each employer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The companies that hire your vocational graduates often have no careers page. The institute's introduction gets me in to build one."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Employers who recruit from the institute already trust it, and many hire without a careers page.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supplier that equips your workshops sells from a PDF catalogue. A trade catalogue with quote requests would win them other training centres."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers sell centre by centre, and the institute's workshop is their reference.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The testing centre where your learners sit certification exams books seats by email. Online exam booking with dates and fees would fix that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Testing venues serve many institutes, and the institute's recommendation brings them more candidates.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each trainer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The freelance trainers who teach your evening courses also run their own workshops. Each needs a booking page that mentions the institute."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Trainers see the institute's new site first-hand and want the same polish for their own work.

withAI.route: Candidate matching assistant for the recruitment agency
withAI.pitchLine: "Graduates of a given training course register, and the agency gets a short summary matched to open roles, with every decision left to recruiters."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agencies screen by hand, and faster shortlists mean faster fees.

withAI.route: Booking assistant for the accommodation provider
withAI.pitchLine: "Learners ask about room types, prices and dates around their course intake, and get an answer and a booking request."
withAI.whyItWorks: Questions come in bursts before each intake, when staff are busiest.

withAI.route: Job description writer for hiring employers
withAI.pitchLine: "A hiring manager describes the vocational role, and gets a clear job post that names the certification and skills the institute trains."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small employers write poor job posts, and better ones bring the right graduates.

withAI.route: Quote assistant for the equipment supplier
withAI.pitchLine: "A training centre describes the courses and class size it runs, and the supplier gets a draft equipment list from its own catalogue to quote."
withAI.whyItWorks: Turning a course outline into a quote takes a sales engineer's time.

withAI.route: Exam booking assistant for the testing venue
withAI.pitchLine: "Candidates ask which certification exam dates have seats and what ID to bring, and get answered and booked from the venue's own rules."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venue staff answer the same questions every exam week.

withAI.route: Workshop enquiry assistant for freelance trainers
withAI.pitchLine: "Prospects ask a trainer about workshop dates, level and price, and get answered and booked while the trainer is teaching."
withAI.whyItWorks: Trainers miss messages in class. A small monthly fee is less than one seat.

softwareAI.name: Enquiry follow-up and advisor call booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every course enquiry gets an instant reply with the fee and next intake, and a slot to book a call with an advisor for that course."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the course list, advisor calendars and the reply wording.

softwareAI.name: Intake seat countdown reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Learners who enquired about a course get a reminder as its intake approaches with the seats left, and a final note before enrolment closes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs intake dates and seat limits per course.

softwareAI.name: Course advisor assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A learner describes their job and goal, and gets the right course, level and next intake from the institute's own catalogue, with a call booking for anything unsure."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the catalogue, entry rules and the director's approval of answers. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Instalment billing and payment reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Learners on a course payment plan get reminders before each instalment, and the finance team sees who is behind without chasing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once instalment enrolments arrive. Needs the payment plans and payment provider.

softwareAI.name: Corporate proposal drafting
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A company's training request becomes a draft proposal with matched courses, delivery options and group pricing, for the corporate lead to edit and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once requests come through the corporate page. Needs past proposals and rate cards. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Enquiry source and enrolment dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enquiries, advisor calls, enrolments and revenue by course, intake and source on one screen, so the institute knows which training campaign filled seats."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after one intake on the new site. Needs the student system's enrolment export.

softwareAI.name: Attendance and certificate issuing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Trainers mark attendance from a tablet, completion rules are checked automatically, and certificates are issued with a verification code."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs completion rules per course and the certificate design.

softwareAI.name: Corporate client portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Companies book training seats for staff, see attendance and completion, and download invoices and certificates themselves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once several corporate clients book regularly. Needs the student system's integration options.

softwareAI.name: Trainer and room scheduling across campuses
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Courses, trainers, workshops and rooms scheduled across campuses without double-booking, with the course timetable published to the site."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs trainer availability, room and workshop lists and the course timetable.

softwareAI.name: Enrolment document checker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Uploaded IDs, transcripts and prior certificates are checked for completeness against each course's entry rules, and admissions makes every decision."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs entry rules and the privacy rules where they operate. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Learner feedback surveys by course
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Learners rate each training module and trainer mid-course and at the end, and results go to the academic lead by course."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the questions and the module list.

softwareAI.name: Next-level course offers for graduates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Graduates get an offer for the next-level course or a related certification when they finish, timed to the next intake."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the course progression map.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the institute
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New reviews of the institute get a reply drafted in its voice that names the course where the reviewer did, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, with the review programme. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Assessment marking assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Written course assessments are pre-checked against the marking guide with draft feedback, and the trainer or assessor makes every final mark."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs marking guides and sample marked work. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Graduate jobs board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Hiring partners post roles for the institute's graduates, and graduates apply with their verified certificate attached to their profile."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, once hiring partners are named. Needs the partners' agreement.

softwareAI.name: Learning platform and site single sign-in
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Learners enrol on the site and land in their online course already signed in, with no second account to create."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs the learning platform's integration options and the IT lead.

softwareAI.name: Student portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "One sign-in for learners: timetable, payments, documents, exam bookings, results and certificates across every course they take."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, when learners juggle several tools. Needs the student system's integration options.

softwareAI.name: Course page and outline writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A trainer's syllabus becomes a draft course page with outcomes, modules and entry requirements, which the academic lead edits and approves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, when new courses are added. Needs syllabus documents. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Corporate training needs survey
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A client company's staff answer a short skills survey, and the institute gets a summary by team to build the training plan from."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 10, for corporate clients planning a full year. Needs the skill areas per course.

softwareAI.name: Enrolment forecast by course and intake
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Forecasts each course's next intake from enquiries, advisor calls and past cohorts, so the institute books trainers and rooms or cancels early."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 12, after several intakes of data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the course catalogue and enrolment for institutes
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a course catalogue with intakes and online enrolment that feeds one institute's student system. Every training centre has the same PDF course list."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Institutes run on a few student systems and identical intake cycles, so one build serves many.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your licensees teach the same courses in different cities with different websites. A shared catalogue where each training centre posts its own intakes keeps the brand consistent."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training brands open centres in new cities and want one standard site.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Institutes teaching different fields, or in other cities, can license the catalogue and corporate funnel we built for a vocational centre in {City}."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Institutes in other fields or cities aren't competitors, so the reference travels.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency white-label of the course catalogue
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "When an education client asks your agency for online enrolment that feeds their student system, resell my course catalogue instead of building it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The enrolment integration is the hard part, and agencies would rather buy it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certification bodies' approved training centre finder
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Learners look for centres approved to teach your certification. A finder fed by each centre's live intake dates sends them to your approved centres."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Certifiers grow by candidate numbers, and a finder that helps centres fill seats helps them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Industry associations and chambers of commerce
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your members need to train staff. A training calendar from member-approved institutes, with group booking, is a reason to renew membership."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations sell membership on practical benefits, and skills are a constant member need.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your reskilling programme sends learners to many providers. A course finder with eligibility checks and enrolment tracking is the build I already run for an institute."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Workforce programmes buy through tenders where a working reference matters most.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your short courses sit inside a university site built for degrees. A course catalogue with intakes and online enrolment fits continuing education exactly."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Continuing education departments are run like institutes and fight their parent site's structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your teams train with several outside providers. A training request and tracking portal across providers is the corporate portal I built for an institute."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: L&D teams want one place to book and report on external training, and the software exists.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Equipment and software vendors' training partner networks
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your product needs certified operators. A training partner finder with each partner's course dates sends customers to the institutes teaching your equipment."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Vendors want trained users, and partner institutes happily list their intakes.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You send learners to vocational institutes abroad. An application tracker where learners see each course offer and its status cuts your email back-and-forth."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agents manage many applications to many institutes, and the institute-side build already exists.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue a broken learning platform migration
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The institute moved to a new learning platform and enrolments from the site stopped creating accounts. I can reconnect them before the next intake."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: An institute losing enrolments in the weeks before an intake pays to fix it fast.

upsellLadder.offer: Institute site and course catalogue plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: The director and the admissions or marketing lead approve the scope.
upsellLadder.line: "The institute site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new course or intake date is one message to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Enquiry follow-up and advisor call booking
upsellLadder.trigger: Course enquiries from the site start waiting a day or more for an advisor reply.
upsellLadder.line: "Every course enquiry can get the fee, next intake and a call slot in the first minute."

upsellLadder.trigger: The next intake has courses with seats left a few weeks out.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's point ads at the training courses with seats left and stop them when each cohort fills."

upsellLadder.trigger: Corporate training requests arrive through the site faster than the sales lead can answer them.
upsellLadder.line: "Each company request can arrive on the corporate lead's desk as a draft proposal, ready to edit."

upsellLadder.trigger: Certificates are still made by hand at the end of each course.
upsellLadder.line: "Attendance marked once, completion checked automatically and a verifiable certificate issued the same day."

upsellLadder.trigger: Several companies book training regularly and ask for attendance reports.
upsellLadder.line: "Your corporate clients can book seats and pull their own attendance and certificates, without emailing the office."

upsellLadder.trigger: Learners complain about separate logins for payments, timetables and results.
upsellLadder.line: "One learner sign-in for timetables, payments and certificates is the next thing every course will feel."
